name: Access Control Policy
description: Defines how identities are established, entitlements are granted, modified, reviewed, and removed, and what authentication is required for access to in-scope systems.
purpose: Give the access controls a documented, approved, and communicated basis, so that the organization's own stated commitments are the standard against which its controls are evaluated.
scope_guidance: Should cover all in-scope systems and every category of identity: employees, contractors, service accounts, shared accounts, administrative accounts, and third-party support access.

required_elements.element: Scope statement identifying the systems and identity types covered
required_elements.rationale: Undefined scope makes it impossible to assess whether a control covered everything it should have.

required_elements.element: Authentication requirements, including where a second factor is required and any permitted exceptions
required_elements.rationale: The policy is what the MFA control is measured against; exceptions must be anticipated in policy rather than improvised.

required_elements.element: Provisioning process with a defined approval authority
required_elements.rationale: Access granted without documented approval is a recurring deficiency.

required_elements.element: Deprovisioning process with a stated timeframe for revocation on termination or role change
required_elements.rationale: The stated timeframe becomes the commitment the organization is held to; without one, timeliness cannot be assessed.

required_elements.element: Access review cadence, reviewer accountability, and required treatment of flagged items
required_elements.rationale: The review control cannot be tested against an undefined cadence, and undefined closure expectations produce reviews with no follow-through.

required_elements.element: Least privilege and segregation of duties principles as applied in this environment
required_elements.rationale: Supports the entitlement-appropriateness judgement reviewers are asked to make.

required_elements.element: Privileged and administrative access handling, including break-glass procedures
required_elements.rationale: Privileged access carries the highest impact and is examined most closely.

required_elements.element: Service account and non-human identity governance, including ownership and credential rotation
required_elements.rationale: Non-human identities are the population most often omitted from access controls.

required_elements.element: Named policy owner, approval record, and review cadence
required_elements.rationale: An unapproved or undated policy is treated as a documentation deficiency.

required_elements.element: Consequences of non-compliance and the exception process
required_elements.rationale: Gives exceptions a governed path instead of silent tolerance.

approval_expectation.approver_role: Executive accountable for security (CISO or equivalent)

communication_expectation: Made available to all personnel with system access and acknowledged at onboarding and on material revision. Relevant to the CC2 communication criteria.
common_gaps: Policy approved after the examination period began, so it did not govern the period it is offered as evidence for.
Deprovisioning timeframe stated in the policy differs from the timeframe the process actually achieves.
Access review cadence in the policy differs from the cadence actually performed.
Service accounts and contractors not addressed at all.

source_refs.supports: The criteria this policy's controls contribute to.
The required_elements model. SOC 2 does not prescribe policy contents.

notes: SOC 2 does not require a document called an Access Control Policy, nor prescribe its contents. 'expected' in required_elements means DriftGuard expects it in a policy that is to support these controls; it is not a SOC 2 requirement.
